cards.title: Introduction to Pandas
cards.content:
Pandas is a fast, powerful, flexible, and easy-to-use open-source data analysis and manipulation tool built on top of the Python programming language.

It introduces two primary data structures: Series (1D) and DataFrame (2D).

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
print(df.head())

content.question: Which of the following represents a 2-dimensional labeled data structure in Pandas?

content.sentence: A one-dimensional labeled array capable of holding any data type in Pandas is called a [blank].

cards.title: Data Manipulation Basics
cards.content:
Once you load data into a DataFrame, you can inspect and manipulate it using built-in methods.

  • df.info(): Provides summary of columns, null counts, and data types.
  • df.describe(): Generates descriptive statistics for numerical columns.
  • df.dropna(): Removes missing values.
  • df.fillna(value): Replaces missing values with a specific value.

steps.text: Load data into a DataFrame using read_csv()
Inspect data structure using head() and info()
Clean data by handling missing values and duplicates

cards.title: Grouping and Aggregation
cards.content:
The groupby method allows you to split data into groups based on some criteria and apply functions to each group.

# Calculate mean salary per department
df.groupby('Department')['Salary'].mean()

You can also use agg() to apply multiple aggregation functions at once.

content.question: What is the primary purpose of the groupby() function in Pandas?

options.text: To merge two different DataFrames together
To split data into groups based on categories for aggregate analysis
To export DataFrame to a CSV file
